headline: Toyota adopts gigacasting in China while Volvo's megacasting launch stumbles

summary.text: Toyota is building a Lexus plant in China with Tesla-style gigacasting, which adds to the risk that OEMs insource body structures such as Lindner's shock towers and longitudinal members.

Volvo's EX60 North American launch is running at 10 percent of target because of megacasting and cell-to-body integration problems, which suggests in-house gigacasting has limits and mid-size castings from suppliers like Lindner may stay in demand.
German automotive takes 32.8% of aluminium consumption as EV production rises 23%, led by Volkswagen, BMW and Mercedes-Benz, which widens the market for Lindner's structural castings.
Speira is investing 40 million euros in aluminium circularity, which could improve recycled-metal supply for the low-CO2 alloys Lindner may need under tightening CO2 requirements.

Inter Foundry & Inter Diecast 2026 offers a venue to meet die-casting peers, tooling suppliers and OEM sourcing contacts. A Hikvision interview describes AI-driven X-ray analysis that could automate porosity detection.

actions.text: Sales lead: use the Volvo EX60 difficulties in talks with OEM contacts to pitch mid-size integrated castings as a lower-risk alternative to full gigacasting.
Purchasing/sustainability lead: contact Speira about recycled and low-carbon aluminium supply volumes and pricing for structural alloys.
Management: decide who attends Inter Diecast and book meetings with tooling suppliers and OEM sourcing contacts. Quality head: ask for an AI X-ray inspection briefing.
